result.summary: Mechanically adds `#include <util/check.h>` and removes `<cassert>` includes across unit test, fuzz, and benchmark files invoking `assert` or `Assert`. Updates the scripted-diff lint environment to allow running `clang-format` and sorts the affected include blocks.
result.problem: Test code relying directly on `<cassert>` or transitive headers creates ambiguity around whether assertions can be stripped by `NDEBUG`. It also causes compilation failures when compiling without assertions in `util/check.h` and complicates automated Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) analysis.
evidence: Commit 9f18b0f183: "The project has a compile error when compiled without assertions in util/check.h. Thus, util/check.h should be included for all assertions."

PR description: "In test code, `assert` is used. This is perfectly fine, but sometimes confusion arises, when it is unclear whether `NDEBUG` can disable the assertions, or whether to use `assert` or `Assert`."
result.scope_notes: A scripted-diff across 154 test and benchmark files, accompanied by a CI lint setup change to install clang-format for scripted-diff checks.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased with no changes to the approach or commit structure.
result.card: Adds explicit `#include <util/check.h>` and drops `<cassert>` via scripted-diff across unit tests, benchmarks, and fuzz harnesses that invoke `assert` or `Assert`. This resolves ambiguity about whether assertions are compiled out by NDEBUG, avoids compile failures when assertions are disabled in `util/check.h`, and facilitates running IWYU tooling. It also enables `clang-format` in the scripted-diff CI verification environment to format and sort headers.

risk.why: Only touches test include lists and a CI lint script; an error would only manifest as a test compilation or CI lint failure.
